source.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch
source.authors: Haoyuan Wu; Ao-Qi Wu; Hai Wang; Jia-Jia Wu; Jinxiang Ou; Bei Yu

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices and tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests compute-optimal scaling in a new setting: native multimodal pre-training from scratch, with separate language and multimodal objectives.
record.gate_note: The study measures smoothed training loss and explicitly uses it as a proxy for test loss; it does not report held-out loss. Downstream evaluations are reported, but they are not measurements of pretraining loss. Results cited from Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study fits offset power-law loss–compute frontiers and IsoFLOP compute-optimal allocation exponents on its own runs. These are 71M–3B activated-parameter MoE models trained from scratch on text and image-text mixtures (r = 0 to 0.3). The r = 0 runs are a plain text-pretraining test, and the r > 0 runs put the same question in a new multimodal setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that per-objective minimal loss follows an offset power law in compute and that compute-optimal N and D scale as powers. Language allocation exponents (≈0.65/0.35) stay similar across mixtures, while the multimodal exponent shifts modestly toward tokens as r rises. They add a budget-compensation rule: the extra compute needed to match pure-text loss is smaller than the multimodal-token compute added. Downstream, aggregate text performance is preserved, text-only spatial reasoning improves, and multimodal in-context learning emerges with scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses IsoFLOP profiles and training-curve envelopes, as in the cited compute-optimal work, but applies them to native multimodal models and objective-specific training losses; the study uses training loss as a test-loss proxy.
record.method_sensitivity: The multimodal allocation exponent changes with multimodal:text token ratio. IsoFLOP and envelope estimates use the same runs and are described as a sensitivity check, not independent validation.

fits_no_version.finding: Inverting a joint text-loss fit (shared offset and exponent) gives Γr ≈ 0.952, 0.915 and 0.899 at r = 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3. Matching pure-text loss needs about 4.7%, 9.8% and 16.9% more total compute, against 10%, 20% and 30% available.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In joint text-image pretraining, the extra multimodal-token compute more than offsets the text-loss efficiency penalty at fixed text loss.

fits_no_version.finding: The multimodal few-shot gain over 0-shot rises from about 0 at A71M to +1.80 at A874M and +2.43 at A3B (Figure 10). Gains appear only in larger models late in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal in-context learning gain grows with model scale and training data in native multimodal pretraining.

record.problems: No held-out loss is measured; smoothed training loss is used as a proxy. Fits are limited to the evaluated model sizes and compute range; the paper notes that some compensation points require extrapolation. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The two allocation estimators use the same training runs and therefore are not independent validation.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many per-benchmark downstream scores and token-by-token training trajectories. Only the aggregate text-benchmark accuracy across model size was retained for V6; the remaining task-level and trajectory results do not measure loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: Scaling beyond about two decades of compute (≈10^19–10^21 FLOPs). Separate laws in N or D with the other factor non-limiting. A held-out set: smoothed single-pass training loss is used instead.
All of it. No small-to-large prediction is validated.
Whether the allocation trend holds beyond the evaluated budgets. IsoFLOP optima are clipped to the 71M–3B observed range.
All of it. Depth and width change together across model sizes; there is no fixed-N shape comparison.
Image or video losses (vision tokens are masked from the loss), repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
Predicting downstream scores from pretraining loss. A fitted or extrapolated downstream scaling law.
Parameter-counting choices, schedules, datasets and fitting methods as varied factors. Numeric IsoFLOP-vs-envelope differences (shown only in figures). Curvature away from a single power law.

missing.what: Aggregate text accuracy versus size at r = 0.1 (22.59→45.50) and r = 0.2 (22.75→45.21)
Envelope-estimator allocation exponents, shown only graphically as a cross-check of the IsoFLOP values

record.verdict_notes: The loss is computed only on text tokens, with vision tokens masked, so 'multimodal loss' means text-token loss in image-text documents. Smoothed training loss stands in for test loss on near single-pass data. No uncertainties or fit-quality statistics are reported. a + b = 1 holds by construction. Separate text fits give offsets of 1.73–1.89 and β of 0.174–0.223 across r, yet the compensation analysis imposes a common offset and β; that modelling choice is not checked. The multimodal characteristic compute scales (≈10^21–10^22) exceed most of the observed compute. Compute coverage is about two decades. N counts activated non-embedding MoE parameters, which matters when comparing the a ≈ 0.65 result with Hoffmann et al.'s 0.5.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss is not measured; smoothed training loss is used as a proxy. The study does not independently establish loss scaling in parameters and tokens with the other factors not bottlenecking.
No validation that fits from smaller runs predict the losses of runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study reports fitted allocation exponents over its evaluated compute range, not validation of the allocation trend over several orders of magnitude beyond that range.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests native multimodal pre-training only; it does not test image/video-only models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling regimes.
Reports downstream accuracy against model size, but does not test prediction from pretraining loss or fit a downstream scaling law.

Tests variation across multimodal data ratios and compares two estimators on the same runs. It does not test parameter-counting choices, alternative schedules or datasets, cross-paper disagreement, or curves bending away from one power law.
